question: A club needs its logo on a phone screen and on a ten-foot banner. Which file should go to the print shop?
option_a: A vector file, because paths stay sharp at any size
option_b: A raster file, because pixels hold detail at large sizes
option_c: A JPEG file, because compression keeps the file small
option_d: A PNG file, because transparency keeps the edges sharp

question: A flyer looks bright on screen, but the printed copies look duller. What is the most likely cause?
option_a: It was designed in RGB, which has colors print cannot match
option_b: It was designed in CMYK, which has colors screens cannot show
option_c: It was exported as a PDF, which removes the bright colors
option_d: It was exported as a PNG, which removes the print colors

question: You squint at your poster and the photo, headline, and date all blur into the same weight. What does that tell you?
option_a: The hierarchy is far too weak
option_b: The contrast is too strong
option_c: The margins are too wide
option_d: The photo is too sharp

question: A poster puts the date at the top, the time at the bottom, and the location in the middle. Which principle fixes this most directly?
option_a: Proximity
option_b: Alignment
option_c: Contrast
option_d: Repetition

question: You must submit your poster for a grade and also show it on your portfolio site. Which pair is right?
option_a: A PDF to submit and a PNG to post
option_b: A PNG to submit and a PDF to post
option_c: The project file to submit and a PNG to post
option_d: A PDF to submit and the project file to post

question: Testers say an app looks beautiful, but most of them cannot figure out how to check out. How would you describe it?
option_a: Strong UI with weak UX
option_b: Strong UX with weak UI
option_c: Weak UI with weak UX
option_d: Strong UI with strong UX

question: You sketched three screens as boxes and labels, then linked them in Figma so a person can click through. You moved from:
option_a: A wireframe to a prototype
option_b: A prototype to a wireframe
option_c: A component to a variant
option_d: A variant to a component

question: A new user opens a to-do app with no tasks yet. What should the screen show?
option_a: A message saying what goes here and how to add one
option_b: A blank screen until the first task is added
option_c: A loading spinner until the first task is added
option_d: A sample list of tasks the user never created

question: A user taps Delete Account. What should appear next?
option_a: A modal asking them to confirm
option_b: A toast saying it was deleted
option_c: A tab bar with more options
option_d: A loading state as it deletes

question: During a user test, the tester gets stuck. You want to point at the right button. What should you do?
option_a: Stay quiet and write down where they got stuck
option_b: Point at the button so the test can keep going
option_c: Explain the screen and let them try once more
option_d: End the test and find a different tester

question: Your navigation bar is a component used on four screens. You change its icon color in the main component. What happens?
option_a: All four instances update
option_b: Only the first instance updates
option_c: Only the main component updates
option_d: All four instances detach

question: A cart was built as four copies of one screen that differ only in the item count. What is the better approach?
option_a: One screen with the count stored in a variable
option_b: Four screens with the count typed on each one
option_c: One screen with the count typed in as text
option_d: Four screens linked together with smart animate

question: A soccer player is blurry at 1/60 in shutter priority. Which change freezes the motion?
option_a: Raise the shutter speed to 1/1000
option_b: Lower the shutter speed to 1/15
option_c: Change the aperture to f/22
option_d: Change the aperture to f/3.5

question: You pan with a walking classmate at 1/500, and the background stays sharp. What is the fix?
option_a: Slow the shutter to about 1/15
option_b: Speed the shutter to about 1/2000
option_c: Open the aperture to about f/3.5
option_d: Close the aperture to about f/22

question: A portrait at f/3.5 still has a sharp wall two feet behind the subject. What is the most effective fix?
option_a: Move the subject farther from the wall
option_b: Move the subject closer to the wall
option_c: Change the aperture to f/16
option_d: Change the ISO to 3200

question: Indoors in aperture priority at f/22, every photo shows camera shake. Why?
option_a: Little light gets in, so the camera picks a slow shutter
option_b: Lots of light gets in, so the camera picks a fast shutter
option_c: Little light gets in, so the camera picks a low ISO
option_d: Lots of light gets in, so the camera picks a high ISO

question: A RAW photo taken under classroom lights looks orange. Which adjustment fixes it?
option_a: Temperature, moved toward blue
option_b: Temperature, moved toward yellow
option_c: Tint, moved toward green
option_d: Tint, moved toward magenta

question: The clipping warning shows red on a small light bulb and on part of the subject's face. What should you do?
option_a: Pull back until the face is clear; the bulb can stay
option_b: Pull back until the bulb is clear; the face can stay
option_c: Leave both, since the warning is only a guide
option_d: Remove both, since any clipping ruins a photo

question: You want a portrait's sky and shirt more colorful without turning the skin orange. Which slider fits best?
option_a: Vibrance
option_b: Saturation
option_c: Clarity
option_d: Dehaze

question: You want a blue sky darker without changing any other color. Which control do you use?
option_a: Blue Luminance, in HSL
option_b: Blue Saturation, in HSL
option_c: Blue Hue, in HSL
option_d: Exposure, in Basic
